preamble.summary: Judith is introduced at last — a wealthy, beautiful, devout widow of impeccable lineage who has lived in seclusion and fasting since her husband's death. Hearing of Uzziah's five-day deadline, she summons the elders and delivers a blistering theological rebuke: no one may put God on trial or set a deadline for the Almighty. She announces she will act — but does not reveal her plan. The elders bless her and depart.
preamble.remarkable: Chapter 8 is Judith's theological manifesto. She does not merely criticize the leaders; she articulates a sophisticated theology of divine sovereignty, testing, and trust. Her speech rivals the finest theological arguments in Job. She is introduced as simultaneously devout, beautiful, wealthy, wise, and courageous — a composite of Israel's ideal virtues.
preamble.friction: Judith's rebuke of the city elders is extraordinarily bold for a woman in this literary context. The narrative presents her authority as self-evident, derived from her piety and wisdom rather than any office.
preamble.connections: Judith's genealogy (traced through many generations) echoes the careful lineages of Genesis and Chronicles. Her widowhood connects her to Tamar, Ruth, and the widow of Zarephath. Her rebuke of 'testing God' draws directly on Deuteronomy 6:16.

verses.text_latin: Et contigit ut audiret haec Iudith vidua quae erat filia Merari filii Idox filii Ioseph filii Oziae filii Elai filii Iamnor filii Gedeon filii Raphaim filii Achitob filii Melchiae filii Enan filii Nathaniae filii Salathiel filii Simeon filii Ruben.
verses.rendering: It happened that these things were heard by Judith, a widow, who was the daughter of Merari, son of Idox, son of Joseph, son of Uzziah, son of Elai, son of Jamnor, son of Gideon, son of Raphaim, son of Achitob, son of Melchiah, son of Enan, son of Nathaniah, son of Salathiel, son of Simeon, son of Reuben.
translator_notes: The elaborate genealogy establishes Judith's deep roots in Israel. Her name, Yehudit ('Jewish woman'), makes her a representative of the entire nation.

key_terms.note: From Hebrew Yehudit — she is 'the Jewish woman' par excellence, embodying the people's identity.

verses.text_latin: Et vir eius fuit Manasses qui mortuus est in diebus messis hordeaceae.
verses.rendering: Her husband was Manasseh, who had died in the days of the barley harvest.
translator_notes: Death during barley harvest — the season of Ruth's arrival in Bethlehem — connects Judith to the tradition of women who act decisively in crisis.

verses.text_latin: Instabat enim super alligantes manipulos in campo et venit aestus super caput eius et mortuus est in Bethulia civitate sua et sepultus est illic cum patribus suis.
verses.rendering: For he was overseeing those binding sheaves in the field, and the heat struck his head, and he died in Bethulia, his city, and was buried there with his fathers.

verses.text_latin: Erat autem Iudith relicta eius vidua iam mensibus tribus et diebus sex.
verses.rendering: Now Judith his widow had been in her widowhood for three years and six months.

verses.text_latin: Et in superioribus domus suae fecit sibi secretum cubiculum in quo cum puellis suis clausa morabatur.
verses.rendering: In the upper part of her house she had made a private chamber for herself, where she remained enclosed with her maidservants.

key_terms.note: Her seclusion is not passive withdrawal but active spiritual discipline — a space of prayer.

verses.text_latin: Et habens super lumbos suos cilicium ieiunabat omnibus diebus vitae suae praeter sabbata et neomenias et festa domus Israhel.
verses.rendering: She wore sackcloth upon her loins and fasted every day of her life, except on sabbaths, new moons, and the feasts of the house of Israel.
translator_notes: Her observance is meticulous — she fasts except when Torah requires feasting. This marks her as someone who submits to God's calendar, not her own preferences.

verses.text_latin: Erat autem eleganti aspectu nimis cui vir suus reliquerat divitias multas et familiam copiosam ac possessiones armentis boum et gregibus ovium plenas.
verses.rendering: She was exceedingly beautiful in appearance, and her husband had left her great wealth, an abundant household, and estates full of herds of cattle and flocks of sheep.

key_terms.note: Her beauty is established before it becomes a weapon — it is a gift she will deploy strategically.

verses.text_latin: Et erat haec in omnibus famosissima quoniam timebat Dominum valde nec erat qui loqueretur de illa verbum malum.
verses.rendering: She was most renowned among all people, because she feared the Lord greatly, and there was no one who spoke an evil word against her.

key_terms.note: The fear of the Lord is her defining characteristic — beauty is secondary to piety.

verses.text_latin: Haec itaque cum audisset quoniam Ozias promisisset quod transacto quinto die traderet civitatem misit ad presbyteros Chabri et Charmi.
verses.rendering: When she heard that Uzziah had promised to surrender the city after the fifth day, she sent for the elders Chabris and Charmi.

verses.text_latin: Et venerunt ad illam et dixit illis quod est hoc verbum in quo consensit Ozias ut tradat civitatem Assyriis si intra quinque dies non venerit adiutorium.
verses.rendering: They came to her, and she said to them: What is this word to which Uzziah has consented — that he would hand over the city to the Assyrians if no help comes within five days?

verses.text_latin: Et qui estis vos qui temptatis Dominum.
verses.rendering: And who are you to put the Lord to the test?
translator_notes: This single sentence is the theological climax of the chapter. It directly invokes the prohibition of Deuteronomy 6:16 ('You shall not put the LORD your God to the test') and Exodus 17:2.

key_terms.rendered_as: put the Lord to the test
key_terms.note: The verb temptare ('to test/tempt') is the exact word used in the Vulgate of Deuteronomy 6:16 and Matthew 4:7.

verses.text_latin: Non est iste sermo qui misericordiam provocet sed potius qui iram excitet et furorem accendat.
verses.rendering: This is not the kind of word that draws down mercy, but rather one that provokes wrath and kindles fury.

verses.text_latin: Posuistis vos tempus miserationis Domini et in arbitrium vestrum diem constituistis ei.
verses.rendering: You have set a time limit on the Lord's compassion and appointed a day for him according to your own judgment.

verses.text_latin: Sed quia patiens Dominus est in hoc ipso paenitentiam agamus et indulgentiam eius fusis lacrimis postulemus.
verses.rendering: But because the Lord is patient, let us repent of this very thing, and with tears streaming, let us beg his forgiveness.

key_terms.note: She appeals to the divine attribute catalog of Exodus 34:6 — the Lord slow to anger.

verses.text_latin: Non enim quasi homo sic Deus commovetur nec sicut filius hominis ad iracundiam inflammabitur.
verses.rendering: For God is not moved as a man is moved, nor kindled to anger as a son of man is.
translator_notes: This verse echoes Numbers 23:19 and 1 Samuel 15:29 — God is not human, subject to mortal moods. Judith's theology is precise and exalted.

verses.text_latin: Et ideo humiliemus illi animas nostras et in spiritu constituti humiliato servientes illi.
verses.rendering: Therefore let us humble our souls before him, and in a spirit of lowliness, let us serve him.

verses.text_latin: Dicamus flentes Domino ut secundum voluntatem suam sic faciat nobiscum misericordiam suam ut sicut conturbatum est cor nostrum in superbia eorum ita etiam de nostra humilitate gloriemur.
verses.rendering: Let us say to the Lord, weeping, that according to his own will he may show us his mercy — so that as our heart has been troubled by their arrogance, so we may glory in our lowliness.

verses.text_latin: Quoniam non secuti sumus peccata patrum nostrorum qui dereliquerunt Deum suum et adoraverunt deos alienos.
verses.rendering: For we have not followed the sins of our fathers who forsook their God and worshipped foreign gods.
translator_notes: A crucial claim: Judith asserts that Israel is currently faithful, which — according to Achior's theology in chapter 5 — means God will defend them.

verses.text_latin: Pro quo scelere dati sunt in gladium et in rapinam et in confusionem inimicis suis nos autem alterum Deum nescimus praeter ipsum.
verses.rendering: For that crime they were given over to the sword, to plunder, and to disgrace before their enemies. But we know no other God besides him.

verses.text_latin: Expectemus humiles consolationem eius et exquiret sanguinem nostrum de adflictionibus inimicorum nostrorum et humiliabit omnes gentes quaecumque insurgunt contra nos et faciet illas sine honore Dominus Deus noster.
verses.rendering: Let us humbly wait for his consolation, and he will require our blood from the afflictions our enemies bring, and he will humble every nation that rises against us, and the Lord our God will make them without honor.

verses.text_latin: Et nunc fratres quoniam vos estis presbyteri in populo Dei et ex vobis pendet anima illorum ad eloquium vestrum corda eorum erigite ut memores sint quia temptati sunt patres nostri ut probarentur si vere colerent Deum suum.
verses.rendering: And now, brothers — since you are elders among the people of God, and their soul hangs upon you, and by your words their hearts are lifted up — remind them that our fathers were tested so that it might be proved whether they truly worshipped their God.
translator_notes: Judith reframes the siege not as punishment but as testing — a profound theological reinterpretation that echoes Deuteronomy 8:2 and the binding of Isaac.

key_terms.rendered_as: were tested so that it might be proved
key_terms.note: Testing as divine pedagogy, not punishment — the same theology as James 1:2-4.

verses.text_latin: Memores esse debent quomodo pater noster Abraham temptatus est et per multas tribulationes probatus Dei amicus effectus est.
verses.rendering: They should remember how our father Abraham was tested, and through many tribulations was proved, and was made a friend of God.

key_terms.note: The title 'friend of God' for Abraham (cf. Isaiah 41:8, James 2:23) — earned through tested faith, not comfort.

verses.text_latin: Sic Isaac sic Iacob sic Moyses et omnes qui placuerunt Deo per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles.
verses.rendering: So Isaac, so Jacob, so Moses, and all who pleased God — they passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful.

verses.text_latin: Illi autem qui tentationes non susceperunt cum timore Domini et impatientiam suam et improperium murmurationis suae contra Dominum protulerunt.
verses.rendering: But those who did not accept their trials with the fear of the Lord, and who brought forth their impatience and the reproach of their murmuring against the Lord —

verses.text_latin: Exterminati sunt ab exterminatore et a serpentibus perierunt.
verses.rendering: They were destroyed by the destroyer and perished by serpents.
translator_notes: Direct reference to Numbers 21:6 (fiery serpents) and 1 Corinthians 10:10 (the destroyer) — murmuring against God in crisis is the sin that kills.

key_terms.note: The destroying angel of the wilderness — the consequence of faithless complaint.

verses.text_latin: Et nos ergo non ulciscamur nos pro his quae patimur.
verses.rendering: Therefore let us not avenge ourselves for what we suffer.

verses.text_latin: Sed reputantes peccatis nostris haec ipsa supplicia minora esse flagella Domini quibus quasi servi corripimur ad emendationem et non ad perditionem nostram evenisse credamus.
verses.rendering: But reckoning these very punishments to be less than our sins deserve, let us believe that these chastisements of the Lord have come upon us for our correction, not our destruction — as upon servants who are disciplined.

key_terms.latin: ad emendationem et non ad perditionem
key_terms.rendered_as: for our correction, not our destruction
key_terms.note: A theology of suffering as divine discipline, echoing Hebrews 12:5-11 and Proverbs 3:11-12.

verses.text_latin: Et dixit ad illam Ozias omnia quae locuta es vera sunt et non est qui contradicat verbis tuis.
verses.rendering: Uzziah said to her: Everything you have spoken is true, and there is no one who can contradict your words.

verses.text_latin: Nec enim hodie primum sapientia tua manifesta est sed ab initio dierum tuorum omnis populus agnovit prudentiam tuam quia bona est dispositio cordis tui.
verses.rendering: For it is not only today that your wisdom has been made manifest, but from the beginning of your days all the people have recognized your prudence, for the disposition of your heart is good.

verses.text_latin: Sed quia sitibat populus compulit nos facere sicuti locuti sumus eis et sacramento nos constrinxit quod praeterire non possumus.
verses.rendering: But because the people were parched with thirst, they compelled us to do as we told them, and bound us by an oath that we cannot break.

verses.text_latin: Et nunc ora pro nobis quoniam mulier sancta es et timens Deum.
verses.rendering: Now therefore pray for us, for you are a holy woman who fears God.

key_terms.latin: mulier sancta es et timens Deum
key_terms.rendered_as: you are a holy woman who fears God
key_terms.note: The elders' acknowledgment of her spiritual authority — the foundation for everything she will do.

verses.text_latin: Et dixit ad illos Iudith sicut quod potui loqui Dei esse cognoscitis.
verses.rendering: Judith said to them: As you recognize that what I have been able to speak is from God,

verses.text_latin: Ita quod facere disposui probate si ex Deo est et orate ut firmum faciat Deus consilium meum.
verses.rendering: So test what I intend to do, whether it is from God, and pray that God may make firm my plan.
translator_notes: She asks them to discern whether her plan is from God — submitting her bold action to communal spiritual discernment.

verses.text_latin: Stabitis vos ad portam nocte ista et ego exeam cum abra mea et orate ut sicut dixistis in diebus quinque respiciat Dominus populum suum Israhel.
verses.rendering: You shall stand at the gate this night, and I will go out with my maidservant. Pray that, as you have said, within five days the Lord may look upon his people Israel.

key_terms.note: Abra (from Greek habra) — a personal attendant, not a slave. This unnamed woman is Judith's companion and co-conspirator throughout.

verses.text_latin: Volo autem ut non scrutemini actum meum et usque dum renuntiem vobis nihil aliud fiat nisi oratio pro me ad Dominum Deum nostrum.
verses.rendering: But I desire that you not inquire into my action, and until I bring you word, let nothing else be done except prayer for me to the Lord our God.
translator_notes: Judith demands operational secrecy and prayer support — a combination of strategic discipline and spiritual dependence.

verses.text_latin: Et dixit ad eam Ozias princeps Iuda vade in pace et Dominus sit tecum in ultionem inimicorum nostrorum et reversi abierunt.
verses.rendering: Uzziah, the prince of Judah, said to her: Go in peace, and may the Lord be with you for the avenging of our enemies. And they turned and departed.
